title: SDK invoker middleware and example patterns for function/tool calls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: implement a language-idiomatic invoker middleware layer across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that centralizes function schema validation, invocation retries (idempotent and non-idempotent paths), streaming resume semantics, and example patterns for integrators. This ticket defines the design, a minimal set of helpers, and canonical examples to reduce copy-paste across projects and improve runtime correctness for function/tool calling use cases.
background: We currently have multiple ad-hoc implementations of function invocation helpers across SDKs that repeat schema coercion logic, have inconsistent retry behavior, and lack unified streaming resume tokens. This causes intermittent customer bugs (schema mismatch errors, double-invokes on retries, broken stream resumes) and increases maintenance burden. Prior work: internal design notes and spike PRs (see attachments).
implementation_notes: Introduce an invoker middleware chain concept: validate -> normalize -> call -> post-validate -> telemetry -> retry-adapter

Provide an idempotency policy abstraction: allow callers to mark functions as idempotent or provide an idempotency key; middleware enforces safe retry if idempotent, otherwise only on safe error classes
Streaming helper: maintain a resumable stream token (opaque KV) produced by runtime that the SDK persists; on reconnect, middleware rehydrates KV cache and requests stream resume with the token
Schema validation strategy: use permissive coercion by default (coerce numbers/strings/booleans where unambiguous), but provide strict mode for enterprise customers via option strict_schema=true
Cross-language primitives: define a small canonical JSON schema for function signatures and a stable serialization format for idempotency keys and resume tokens
Telemetry: emit span and event with fields: function_name, schema_version, invocation_id, retry_count, resume_token_present, runtime_variant
Backpressure for streaming: TS/Python use async iterators with buffered prefetch size; Go uses channel-based ring buffer with configurable capacity
Compatibility: never break old callers — default behavior must remain backward-compatible with existing SDK invocations
Testing: add property-based tests to fuzz schema coercion, end-to-end tests with local runtime to validate resume semantics, and performance microbenchmarks for latency/CPU overhead
Docs & Examples: three canonical examples (Python sync/async, TS with streaming and function calling, Go idiomatic example) to be included in quickstarts
acceptance_criteria: Middleware implemented in Python/TS/Go with the same semantics surface (same option names and default behaviors)
Unit & integration tests cover schema coercion edge cases and resume+retry interaction (>= 95% coverage for new modules)
Three SDK examples added to the docs repo: python-invoker-async, ts-invoker-streaming, go-invoker-idempotent
Telemetry events emitted for every invocation and incorporated into tracing dashboard (link in attachments)
Performance regression < 3% p50 latency for non-streaming calls, and documented overhead for streaming helpers
Design doc reviewed by runtime and SDK leads and PRs merged into main branch
